reuse.why: Adds one shared skipsWeekendOccurrences predicate and routes getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and the budget template through it, keeping getDateWithSkippedWeekend for the non-daily case.

duplication.why: Dropping weekend occurrences is implemented twice: getNextWeekdayOccurrence in shared/schedules (14-occurrence window, find) and an inline over-fetch/filter/slice in getUpcomingDates (count*7 window).

placement.why: Predicate and next-date logic sit in shared/schedules where the weekend rules live; the upcoming-dates drop logic stays in the server handler instead of a shared function.

scope.why: Only the weekend rule, the frequency passed into the recur data, tests and a release note are touched.

maintainability.why: schedule-template repurposes getNextDate's noSkipWeekend flag (now computed as !skipsWeekendOccurrences) so a daily schedule is filtered inside getNextDate and then still passed through getDateWithSkippedWeekend, which is hard to follow; two different scan bounds for the same rule can diverge.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Callers use the shared predicate; getUpcomingDates writes its own filter rather than bypassing an existing helper.

disguised_duplication.where: server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates re-implements getNextWeekdayOccurrence's weekday filtering as a filter/slice chain with a different window size.

one_place.where: Whether the rule applies is decided once (skipsWeekendOccurrences), but how weekend occurrences are dropped is implemented separately in shared/schedules getNextWeekdayOccurrence and server/schedules/app.ts getUpcomingDates, with schedule-template relying on a flag trick through getNextDate.
